owasp-api-top10.title: OWASP API Security Top 10
owasp-api-top10.attribution: OWASP API Security Project. Identifiers and risk titles are referenced from the 2023 edition, which is published by OWASP under CC BY-SA 4.0. The 'look_at' and 'suggests' fields are VardrRunner's own notes, not OWASP text.

items.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
items.look_at: Per-object access: can one identity read or change another's object by changing an id? This is what a VardrGate case tests directly, one operation and several identities at a time.

items.title: Broken Authentication
items.look_at: Credential handling, token issuance, expiry and refresh. Nothing here exercises an authentication flow end to end; a scanner finding is at best a hint.

items.title: Broken Object Property Level Authorization
items.look_at: Field-level reads and writes within an object an identity may otherwise access: mass assignment, and properties returned that the caller should not see. Needs crafted requests and a view of what each field means.

items.title: Unrestricted Resource Consumption
items.look_at: Absent rate limits, unbounded page sizes, expensive operations. No job type here measures this, and VardrRunner's own rate caps are restraints on our traffic, not a test of the target's.

items.title: Broken Function Level Authorization
items.look_at: Whether an identity can call an operation reserved for another role. A VardrGate case with one identity per role and an explicit decision per identity is the direct test.

items.title: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
items.look_at: Flows that are individually authorized but harmful in bulk â€” checkout, invite, password reset. Identifying which flows matter is a conversation with the client, not a scan.

items.title: Server Side Request Forgery
items.look_at: Parameters the server fetches on your behalf. nuclei carries SSRF templates, so a match is real evidence of a candidate; absence of a match is not evidence of absence.

items.title: Security Misconfiguration
items.look_at: Headers, TLS, verbose errors, exposed debug and admin surfaces, permissive CORS. httpx fingerprints, nuclei matches known misconfigurations, nmap and naabu show what is listening.

items.title: Improper Inventory Management
items.look_at: Hosts, versions and operations nobody is tracking â€” old /v1 still live, staging reachable, undocumented endpoints. The engagement's own API surface and recon inventory are the evidence here.

items.title: Unsafe Consumption of APIs
items.look_at: What the target trusts from third-party APIs it calls. This is largely a code and architecture question and is not reachable from outside.

owasp-wstg.title: OWASP Web Security Testing Guide
owasp-wstg.attribution: OWASP Web Security Testing Guide v4.2, published by OWASP under CC BY-SA 4.0. Section numbers and category titles are referenced from the guide; the 'look_at' and 'suggests' fields are VardrRunner's own notes, not OWASP text. These are the twelve top-level categories, not the individual tests within them.

items.title: Information Gathering
items.look_at: What exists and what it runs. This is the part of the guide the runner covers best: subdomains, live hosts, crawled endpoints, archived URLs, discovered paths.

items.title: Configuration and Deployment Management Testing
items.look_at: Exposed admin interfaces, old files, directory listings, HTTP methods, platform defaults. Port and service discovery plus template matching cover a good share of this.

items.title: Identity Management Testing
items.look_at: Registration, provisioning, role definitions, username policy. Needs accounts and a view of the roles the application intends.

items.title: Authentication Testing
items.look_at: Credentials over the wire, lockout, password reset, remember-me, cached logins. Hands-on; no job type here walks a login flow.

items.title: Authorization Testing
items.look_at: Directory traversal, privilege escalation, insecure direct object references. A VardrGate case is the repeatable form of this for API operations.

items.title: Session Management Testing
items.look_at: Cookie attributes, fixation, timeout, logout, CSRF. Needs a live session to observe.

items.title: Input Validation Testing
items.look_at: Injection of every kind, plus XSS. nuclei matches known patterns; anything beyond that is manual until a dedicated fuzzer is wired in.

items.title: Testing for Error Handling
items.look_at: Stack traces and messages that disclose internals. Crawled and fuzzed responses are where these turn up, but recognising one is a judgement.

items.title: Testing for Weak Cryptography
items.look_at: TLS versions and ciphers, weak algorithms, padding oracles. Service detection and templates cover the transport layer.

items.title: Business Logic Testing
items.look_at: Workflow circumvention, request timing, upload abuse. Requires understanding what the application is for; no scanner finds this.

items.title: Client-side Testing
items.look_at: DOM XSS, client-side injection, postMessage, CORS from the browser's side. Crawling with JavaScript parsing finds the surface; confirming a client-side issue is manual.

items.title: API Testing
items.look_at: The API as its own surface. Pair this with the OWASP API Security Top 10, which goes into far more detail, and with the engagement's API operation inventory.
